title: Conservative FP8 fallback orchestrator and calibration runbook for Hopper (E4M3/E5M2)
creator: Liam Chen
description: Enable a conservative FP8 serving path for Hopper GPUs that prioritizes correctness and predictable degradation. Deliverables: (1) per-shard runtime fallback layer that can revert shards to INT8/FP16 automatically, (2) an orchestrator service to coordinate calibration runs and golden-vector replays, (3) telemetry gating and a drift detector to prevent silent accuracy regressions, and (4) a documented ops runbook with canary recipe and rollback criteria.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Runtime exposes per-shard quant mode with unsafe-mode flag disabled by default
A2: Orchestrator can schedule and complete a calibration job across a 64-shard Hopper pool and publish per-shard thresholds
A3: Shadow traffic harness runs against FP8 path with automated comparison to golden outputs; nightlies produce a regression report
A4: Drift detector raises an alert when KL-divergence or top-k mismatch exceed configured thresholds for 3 consecutive windows
A5: Canary rollout automation can shift weight away from FP8 path off a model if the SLO or quality metric breaches defined gates
A6: Ops runbook and an automated rollback playbook validated by a simulated incident drill

playbook_steps: Step 0: Validate signal quality — confirm golden-vector baseline run is available and passes checksum
Step 1: Run orchestrator calibration job on a small shard subset (n=4) in shadow mode
Step 2: Collect per-op statistics and compute drift metrics (KL, top-k mismatch, token-level edit distance)
Step 3: If any shard exceeds soft-thresholds, mark shard for hysteresis and schedule a re-calibration
Step 4: If shard exceeds hard-thresholds, flip shard to INT8/FP16 fallback and emit incident with proposed remediation
Step 5: Execute canary rollout with weight ramp (1% -> 10% -> 50%) while monitoring quality and latency SLOs
Step 6: If canary fails, run automated rollback and trigger postmortem drill
